data.name: Ardhika
data.gender_notes: Ardhika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Ardhika represents the half or part of something. It can refer to the god Ardhanarishwar, who is half Shiva and half Parvati, symbolizing the unity of masculine and feminine energies. The name Ardhika carries the meaning “Half, Part” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ardhika usually hope their child will grow to embody half, part and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the balance between opposites and the unity of all elements.
data.etymology: Ardhika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Half, Part.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ardhika total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ardhika holds significance in Hindu culture as it is a name associated with wholeness and completeness, derived from the concept of being half or part of something greater. This can be seen in various aspects of Hindu society and mythology, such as festivals, rituals, and symbols. For instance, the Hindu calendar includes a month called Ardha-Paksha, which is the fortnight of waning moon. This term signifies a transition period from the full moon to the new moon, emphasizing the importance of completeness and transformation.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Ardhika holds profound meaning representing the unity of opposites and the harmony of masculine and feminine energies within the divine being. Ardhanareshwar, a form of Shiva, symbolizes this concept, embodying the god in his half-man and half-woman form. This symbolizes the balance and integration of the dual nature of the universe, where Shiva, the destructor, and Parvati, the creator and nurturer, merge as one. Embracing the name Ardhika can serve as a reminder of the importance of seeking a balanced and harmonious existence within oneself and in one's relationships.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ardhika symbolizes the harmonious blend of dualities - inner and outer, light and dark, masculine and feminine. It represents the journey towards self-realization, where one strives to balance these opposites within and achieve inner peace.

historical_references.reference: Ardhika was a popular name for girls during the Gupta Empire (320-550 AD) in India. It is believed to have derived from the Sanskrit word 'ardhika' which means 'middle' or 'central'. The name was given to girls born in the middle of the lunar month or those who were considered to be the center of their families.
historical_references.context: Gupta Empire, India, popular name for girls, derived from Sanskrit word 'ardhika' meaning 'middle' or 'central'

historical_references.reference: Another historical reference indicates that Ardhika was an alternative name for the Hindu goddess Shakti during the medieval period (500-1300 AD) in India. Shakti is the divine feminine energy and consort of Shiva, and Ardhika is believed to represent the fierce and powerful aspect of the goddess.
historical_references.context: Medieval period, India, alternative name for Hindu goddess Shakti, represents fierce and powerful aspect
